messages.author: 487e92c15ae8f858
messages.subject: grid.locator() in shiny webapp?
parts:
In R the grid.locator() function will deliver coordinates for mouse clicks. 
I'm currently attempting to produce this functionality on the UI (client) side of a shiny using HTML5 canvas.
http://www.html5canvastutorials.com/advanced/html5-canvas-mouse-coordinates/
Is there some way to link this back to the server in such a way that grid graphics can translate to plot coordinates?
Thanks!
-Ryan

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: grid.locator() in shiny webapp?
parts: There's not a great way right now. You can get the pixel coordinates back to the server, but reactivePlot opens and closes the graphics device, so the data we would need to support this is already gone. This doesn't seem like an inherently unsolvable problem but I don't currently have a solution--I'm not that familiar with the R graphics subsystems so if you have ideas, let me know.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: grid.locator() in shiny webapp?
parts:
Prompted by Susan and Yihui, I decided to take a quick look at this and found the R graphics devices to be much simpler than I had expected!

Here's a proposed implementation:

devtools::install_github("shiny", "jcheng5", ref="plot-mouse-events")

This adds two new parameters to plotOutput: clickId and hoverId. If you provide names for them, they will start providing reactive values under those names in the usual way. The values will have x and y (or the whole value may be NULL if the plot has never been clicked, or the plot is not currently being hovered over). And importantly, the x and y values will be in user coordinates, not pixels!

Example:
https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/5835269
shiny::runGist("https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/5835269")

The main thing I know doesn't work right now (at least it shouldn't) is that you will get funky results on Retina displays. It should be a straightforward fix.

Also, I know it doesn't work on ggplot2 plots (though locator() doesn't work on ggplot2 either).

Please try it and let us know if it works, especially on funkier graphs. If you find any graphs where locator() works but this doesn't, let us know!

On Fri, Jun 21, 2013 at 1:13 PM, Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com> wrote:
My guess is some JavaScript hacks to obtain pixel coordinates +
graphics::grconvertX(from = 'device')/grconvertY() would probably
work, although that is much less straightforward than locator().

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: grid.locator() in shiny webapp?
parts:
This is so awesome! Now I can smell a lot of interesting interactive
graphics applications approaching. We, just, need, this, right, now!
:)

It will be even more awesome if mousedown/mouseup events can
supported. Then we will be able to select elements in a region, and
that is an important step to interactive graphics. But it actually
suffices to have click and hover only, e.g. we can click twice to
define a region. It is just a matter of user experience.

Regards,
Yihui
--

parts:
I've just had a chance to sit down and play with this. There is a gglocator() function in the ggmaps package, just fyi, but I'm not quite sure how it works. 

It seems that when using par() to put multiple graphs in one output plot, the click and hover coordinates are off. 

Example: https://gist.github.com/srvanderplas/d5f3bfdd756f1dfe39c1
Shiny App: http://vanderplas.dyndns-remote.com:3838/AppStat/14-outlier-clickable/

using locator() on the same graph in R returns accurate values.
On Fri, Jun 21, 2013 at 7:21 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:

Prompted by Susan and Yihui, I decided to take a quick look at this and found the R graphics devices to be much simpler than I had expected!

Here's a proposed implementation:

devtools::install_github("shiny", "jcheng5", ref="plot-mouse-events")

This adds two new parameters to plotOutput: clickId and hoverId. If you provide names for them, they will start providing reactive values under those names in the usual way. The values will have x and y (or the whole value may be NULL if the plot has never been clicked, or the plot is not currently being hovered over). And importantly, the x and y values will be in user coordinates, not pixels!

Example:
https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/5835269
shiny::runGist("https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/5835269")

The main thing I know doesn't work right now (at least it shouldn't) is that you will get funky results on Retina displays. It should be a straightforward fix.

Also, I know it doesn't work on ggplot2 plots (though locator() doesn't work on ggplot2 either).

Please try it and let us know if it works, especially on funkier graphs. If you find any graphs where locator() works but this doesn't, let us know!

work, although that is much less straightforward than locator().

Yihui

This has been a major blessing for one of my projects.
Thanks, Joe!

A note on zooming:

It seems that in Safari, if you zoom the window
(double-tap or reverse-pinch),
the coordinates returned by hover are no longer correct.
However, using Chrome, zooming does not affect the coordinates
returned-- they are fine.

This is with vanilla plot.default().
I'm on OSX Yosemite.
